narrative:
The model estimated a 63% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, so your application was denied. This means that, based on the information supplied, the model judged bad repayment to be more likely than not; it is not a statement that default is certain.

The strongest reason was your checking-account position: a balance in the 0–200 DM range is relatively uncommon among approved applicants, and this was the largest factor pushing the decision toward denial. The next strongest factor was that no property was recorded. Approved applicants usually show some property or collateral, and only about 8% have none, so this lack of recorded assets also pushed toward bad risk. Third, the requested credit period was 36 months, well above the approved average of about 19 months. A longer commitment increased the model’s concern and pushed further toward denial.

To improve a future application, consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter repayment period, providing documented savings, assets, or collateral, and strengthening your checking-account position. You could also ask the lender what specific evidence would update your profile, then reapply when those circumstances have changed.
